Name: InverseChiSquareDistribution
PlaintextUsage:
InverseChiSquareDistribution[ν] represents an inverse χ^2 distribution with ν degrees of freedom.
InverseChiSquareDistribution[ν, ξ] represents a scaled inverse χ^2 distribution with ν degrees of freedom and scale ξ.

Name: InverseContinuousWaveletTransform
PlaintextUsage:
InverseContinuousWaveletTransform[cwd] gives the inverse continuous wavelet transform of a ContinuousWaveletData object cwd. 
InverseContinuousWaveletTransform[cwd, wave] gives the inverse transform using the wavelet wave.
InverseContinuousWaveletTransform[cwd, wave, octvoc] gives the inverse transform from the wavelet coefficients specified by octvoc.

Name: InverseDistanceTransform
PlaintextUsage: InverseDistanceTransform[image] gives the inverse distance transform of image, returning the result as a binary image.

Name: InverseEllipticNomeQ
PlaintextUsage: InverseEllipticNomeQ[q] gives the parameter m corresponding to the nome q in an elliptic function.

Name: InverseErf
PlaintextUsage: InverseErf[s] gives the inverse error function obtained as the solution for z in s=erf (z).

Name: InverseErfc
PlaintextUsage: InverseErfc[s] gives the inverse complementary error function obtained as the solution for z in s=erfc (z).

Name: InverseFourier
PlaintextUsage:
InverseFourier[list] finds the discrete inverse Fourier transform of a list of complex numbers.
InverseFourier[list, {p1, p2, …}] returns the specified positions of the discrete inverse Fourier transform.

Name: InverseFourierCosTransform
PlaintextUsage:
InverseFourierCosTransform[expr, ω, t] gives the symbolic inverse Fourier cosine transform of expr. 
InverseFourierCosTransform[expr, {ω1, ω2, …}, {t1, t2, …}] gives the multidimensional inverse Fourier cosine transform of expr.

Name: InverseFourierSequenceTransform
PlaintextUsage:
InverseFourierSequenceTransform[expr, ω, n] gives the inverse discrete-time Fourier transform of expr.
InverseFourierSequenceTransform[expr, {ω1, ω2, …}, {n1, n2, …}] gives the multidimensional inverse Fourier sequence transform.

Name: InverseFourierSinTransform
PlaintextUsage:
InverseFourierSinTransform[expr, ω, t] gives the symbolic inverse Fourier sine transform of expr. 
InverseFourierSinTransform[expr, {ω1, ω2, …}, {t1, t2, …}] gives the multidimensional inverse Fourier sine transform of expr.

Name: InverseFourierTransform
PlaintextUsage:
InverseFourierTransform[expr, ω, t] gives the symbolic inverse Fourier transform of expr. 
InverseFourierTransform[expr, {ω1, ω2, …}, {t1, t2, …}] gives the multidimensional inverse Fourier transform of expr.

Name: InverseFunction
PlaintextUsage:
InverseFunction[f] represents the inverse of the function f, defined so that InverseFunction[f][y] gives the value of x for which f[x] is equal to y. 
InverseFunction[f, n, tot] represents the inverse with respect to the n ^th argument when there are tot arguments in all.

Name: InverseFunctions
PlaintextUsage: InverseFunctions is an option for Solve and related functions that specifies whether inverse functions should be used.

Name: InverseGammaDistribution
PlaintextUsage:
InverseGammaDistribution[α, β] represents an inverse gamma distribution with shape parameter α and scale parameter β.
InverseGammaDistribution[α, β, γ, μ] represents a generalized inverse gamma distribution with shape parameters α and γ, scale parameter β, and location parameter μ.

Name: InverseGammaRegularized
PlaintextUsage: InverseGammaRegularized[a, s] gives the inverse of the regularized incomplete gamma function.

Name: InverseGaussianDistribution
PlaintextUsage:
InverseGaussianDistribution[μ, λ] represents an inverse Gaussian distribution with mean μ and scale parameter λ.
InverseGaussianDistribution[μ, λ, θ] represents a generalized inverse Gaussian distribution with parameters μ, λ, and θ.

Name: InverseGudermannian
PlaintextUsage: InverseGudermannian[z] gives the inverse Gudermannian function gd^-1 (z).

Name: InverseHankelTransform
PlaintextUsage:
InverseHankelTransform[expr, s, r] gives the inverse Hankel transform of order 0 for expr.
InverseHankelTransform[expr, s, r, ν] gives the inverse Hankel transform of order ν for expr.

Name: InverseHaversine
PlaintextUsage: InverseHaversine[z] gives the inverse haversine function hav^-1 (z).

Name: InverseHilbertTransform
PlaintextUsage:
InverseHilbertTransform[F[t], t, s] gives the symbolic inverse Hilbert transform of F[t] in the variable t and returns a transform f[s] in the variable s.
InverseHilbertTransform[F[t], t, Overscript[s, ^]] gives the numeric inverse Hilbert transform at the numerical value Overscript[s, ^].

Name: InverseImagePyramid
PlaintextUsage:
InverseImagePyramid[pyr] reconstructs an image from an ImagePyramid object pyr.
InverseImagePyramid[pyr, pyrtype] assumes the specified pyramid type pyrtype.
InverseImagePyramid[pyr, pyrtype, n] reconstructs up to pyramid level n.
InverseImagePyramid[pyr, pyrtype, {size}] reconstructs up to the smallest pyramid level larger than the specified size.

Name: InverseJacobiCD
PlaintextUsage: InverseJacobiCD[v, m] gives the inverse Jacobi elliptic function cd^-1 (vm).

Name: InverseJacobiCN
PlaintextUsage: InverseJacobiCN[v, m] gives the inverse Jacobi elliptic function cn^-1 (vm).

Name: InverseJacobiCS
PlaintextUsage: InverseJacobiCS[v, m] gives the inverse Jacobi elliptic function cs^-1 (vm).

Name: InverseJacobiDC
PlaintextUsage: InverseJacobiDC[v, m] gives the inverse Jacobi elliptic function dc^-1 (vm).

Name: InverseJacobiDN
PlaintextUsage: InverseJacobiDN[v, m] gives the inverse Jacobi elliptic function dn^-1 (vm).

Name: InverseJacobiDS
PlaintextUsage: InverseJacobiDS[v, m] gives the inverse Jacobi elliptic function ds^-1 (vm).

Name: InverseJacobiNC
PlaintextUsage: InverseJacobiNC[v, m] gives the inverse Jacobi elliptic function nc^-1 (vm).

Name: InverseJacobiND
PlaintextUsage: InverseJacobiND[v, m] gives the inverse Jacobi elliptic function nd^-1 (vm).

Name: InverseJacobiNS
PlaintextUsage: InverseJacobiNS[v, m] gives the inverse Jacobi elliptic function ns^-1 (vm).

Name: InverseJacobiSC
PlaintextUsage: InverseJacobiSC[v, m] gives the inverse Jacobi elliptic function sc^-1 (vm).

Name: InverseJacobiSD
PlaintextUsage: InverseJacobiSD[v, m] gives the inverse Jacobi elliptic function sd^-1 (vm).

Name: InverseJacobiSN
PlaintextUsage: InverseJacobiSN[v, m] gives the inverse Jacobi elliptic function sn^-1 (vm).

Name: InverseLaplaceTransform
PlaintextUsage:
InverseLaplaceTransform[F[s], s, t] gives the symbolic inverse Laplace transform of F[s] in the variable s as f[t] in the variable t. 
InverseLaplaceTransform[F[s], s, Overscript[t, ^]] gives the numeric inverse Laplace transform at the numerical value Overscript[t, ^].
InverseLaplaceTransform[F[s1, …, sn], {s1, s2, …}, {t1, t2, …}] gives the multidimensional inverse Laplace transform of F[s1, …, sn].

Name: InverseMellinTransform
PlaintextUsage: InverseMellinTransform[expr, s, x] gives the inverse Mellin transform of expr.

Name: InversePermutation
PlaintextUsage: InversePermutation[perm] returns the inverse of permutation perm.

Name: InverseRadon
PlaintextUsage:
InverseRadon[image] gives the inverse discrete Radon transform of image.
InverseRadon[image, {w, h}] specifies the width w and the height h of the resulting image.

Name: InverseRadonTransform
PlaintextUsage: InverseRadonTransform[expr, {p, ϕ}, {x, y}] gives the inverse Radon transform of expr.

Name: InverseSeries
PlaintextUsage:
InverseSeries[s] takes the series s, and gives a series for the inverse of the function represented by s. 
InverseSeries[s, x] uses the variable x in the inverse series.

Name: InverseShortTimeFourier
PlaintextUsage:
InverseShortTimeFourier[input] reconstructs the signal from short-time Fourier data.
InverseShortTimeFourier[input, n] assumes the spectrogram data was computed with partitions of length n.
InverseShortTimeFourier[input, n, d] assumes partitions with offset d.
InverseShortTimeFourier[input, n, d, wfun] assumes a smoothing window wfun was applied to each partition.

Name: InverseSpectrogram
PlaintextUsage:
InverseSpectrogram[data] reconstructs the signal from the magnitude spectrogram data.
InverseSpectrogram[img] reconstructs the signal, assuming that the image img is the magnitude spectrogram.
InverseSpectrogram[input, n] assumes the spectrogram data was computed with partitions of length n.
InverseSpectrogram[input, n, d] assumes partitions with offset d.
InverseSpectrogram[input, n, d, wfun] assumes a smoothing window wfun was applied to each partition.

Name: InverseSurvivalFunction
PlaintextUsage: InverseSurvivalFunction[dist, q] gives the inverse of the survival function for the distribution dist as a function of the variable q.

Name: InverseTransformedRegion
PlaintextUsage: InverseTransformedRegion[reg, f, n] represents the inverse transformed region {p∈^n|f(p)∈reg}, where reg is a region and f is a function.

Name: InverseWaveletTransform
PlaintextUsage:
InverseWaveletTransform[dwd] gives the inverse wavelet transform of a DiscreteWaveletData object dwd.
InverseWaveletTransform[dwd, wave] gives the inverse transform using the wavelet wave.
InverseWaveletTransform[dwd, wave, wind] gives the inverse transform from the wavelet coefficients specified by wind.

Name: InverseWeierstrassP
PlaintextUsage: InverseWeierstrassP[p, {g2, g3}] gives a value of u for which the Weierstrass function ℘(u;g2, g3) is equal to p.

Name: InverseWishartMatrixDistribution
PlaintextUsage: InverseWishartMatrixDistribution[ν, Σ] represents an inverse Wishart matrix distribution with ν degrees of freedom and covariance matrix Σ.

Name: InverseZTransform
PlaintextUsage:
InverseZTransform[expr, z, n] gives the inverse Z transform of expr. 
InverseZTransform[expr, {z1, …, zm}, {n1, …, nm}] gives the multiple inverse Z transform of expr.

Name: Invisible
PlaintextUsage: Invisible[expr] displays as space that is the same size as the formatted version of expr.

Name: IrreduciblePolynomialQ
PlaintextUsage:
IrreduciblePolynomialQ[poly] tests whether poly is an irreducible polynomial over the rationals.
IrreduciblePolynomialQ[poly, Modulusp] tests whether poly is irreducible modulo a prime p.
IrreduciblePolynomialQ[poly, Extension{a1, a2, …}] tests whether poly is irreducible over the field extension generated by the algebraic numbers ai.
IrreduciblePolynomialQ[poly, ExtensionAll] tests whether poly is absolutely irreducible over the complex numbers.

Name: IslandData
PlaintextUsage:
IslandData[entity, property] gives the value of the specified property for the island entity.
IslandData[{entity1, entity2, …}, property] gives a list of property values for the specified island entities.
IslandData[entity, property, annotation] gives the specified annotation associated with the given property.

Name: IsolatingInterval
PlaintextUsage:
IsolatingInterval[a] gives a rational isolating interval for the algebraic number a.
IsolatingInterval[a, dx] gives an isolating interval of width at most dx.

Name: IsomorphicGraphQ
PlaintextUsage: IsomorphicGraphQ[g1, g2] yields True if the graphs g1 and g2 are isomorphic, and False otherwise.

Name: IsomorphicSubgraphQ
PlaintextUsage: IsomorphicSubgraphQ[g1, g2] yields True if the graph g1 is isomorphic to a subgraph of the graph g2.

Name: IsotopeData
PlaintextUsage:
IsotopeData[{Z, A}, "property"] gives the value of the specified property for the isotope with atomic number Z and mass number A.
IsotopeData["name", "property"] gives the value of the property for the named isotope.

Name: Italic
PlaintextUsage: Italic represents an italic font slant.

Name: Item
PlaintextUsage: Item[expr, options] represents an item within constructs such as Grid, Overlay, and Manipulate that displays with expr as the content, and with the specified options applied to the region containing expr.

Name: ItemAspectRatio
PlaintextUsage: ItemAspectRatio is an option for GraphicsGrid which specifies the ratio of height to width for the regions in which items are placed in the graphics grid.

Name: ItemDisplayFunction
PlaintextUsage: ItemDisplayFunction is an option for Dataset that specifies a function to apply to items before displaying them.

Name: ItemSize
PlaintextUsage: ItemSize is an option for Grid, Column, and related constructs that specifies the sizes to allow for items.

Name: ItemStyle
PlaintextUsage: ItemStyle is an option for Dataset, Grid and related constructs that specifies styles to use for items.

Name: ItoProcess
PlaintextUsage:
ItoProcess[{a, b}, x, t] represents an Ito process x(t), where x(t)a(t, x(t))t+b (t, x(t)).w(t).
ItoProcess[{a, b, c}, x, t] represents an Ito process y(t)c(t, x(t)), where x(t)a(t, x(t))t+b (t, x(t)).w(t) .
ItoProcess[…, {x, x0}, {t, t0}] uses initial condition x(t0)x0.
ItoProcess[…, …, …, Σ] uses a Wiener process w(t), with covariance Σ.
ItoProcess[proc] converts proc to a standard Ito process whenever possible. 
ItoProcess[sdeqns, expr, x, t, wdproc] represents an Ito process specified by a stochastic differential equation sdeqns, output expression expr, with state x and time t, driven by w following the process dproc.

Name: JaccardDissimilarity
PlaintextUsage: JaccardDissimilarity[u, v] gives the Jaccard dissimilarity between Boolean vectors u and v.

Name: JacobiAmplitude
PlaintextUsage: JacobiAmplitude[u, m] gives the amplitude am(um) for Jacobi elliptic functions.

Name: JacobiCD
PlaintextUsage: JacobiCD[u, m] gives the Jacobi elliptic function cd (u|m).

Name: JacobiCN
PlaintextUsage: JacobiCN[u, m] gives the Jacobi elliptic function cn (u|m).

Name: JacobiCS
PlaintextUsage: JacobiCS[u, m] gives the Jacobi elliptic function cs (u|m).

Name: JacobiDC
PlaintextUsage: JacobiDC[u, m] gives the Jacobi elliptic function dc (u|m).

Name: JacobiDN
PlaintextUsage: JacobiDN[u, m] gives the Jacobi elliptic function dn (u|m).

Name: JacobiDS
PlaintextUsage: JacobiDS[u, m] gives the Jacobi elliptic function ds (u|m).

Name: JacobiEpsilon
PlaintextUsage: JacobiEpsilon[u, m] gives the Jacobi epsilon function ℰ (um).

Name: JacobiNC
PlaintextUsage: JacobiNC[u, m] gives the Jacobi elliptic function nc (u|m).

Name: JacobiND
PlaintextUsage: JacobiND[u, m] gives the Jacobi elliptic function nd (u|m).

Name: JacobiNS
PlaintextUsage: JacobiNS[u, m] gives the Jacobi elliptic function ns (u|m).

Name: JacobiP
PlaintextUsage: JacobiP[n, a, b, x] gives the Jacobi polynomial P _n^(a, b)(x).

Name: JacobiSC
PlaintextUsage: JacobiSC[u, m] gives the Jacobi elliptic function sc (u|m).

Name: JacobiSD
PlaintextUsage: JacobiSD[u, m] gives the Jacobi elliptic function sd (u|m).

Name: JacobiSN
PlaintextUsage: JacobiSN[u, m] gives the Jacobi elliptic function sn (um).

Name: JacobiSymbol
PlaintextUsage: JacobiSymbol[n, m] gives the Jacobi symbol (n/m).

Name: JacobiZN
PlaintextUsage: JacobiZN[u, m] gives the Jacobi zeta function zn (um).

Name: JacobiZeta
PlaintextUsage: JacobiZeta[ϕ, m] gives the Jacobi zeta function Ζ (ϕm).

Name: JankoGroupJ1
PlaintextUsage: JankoGroupJ1[] represents the sporadic simple Janko group J1.

Name: JankoGroupJ2
PlaintextUsage: JankoGroupJ2[] represents the sporadic simple Janko group J2.

Name: JankoGroupJ3
PlaintextUsage: JankoGroupJ3[] represents the sporadic simple Janko group J3.

Name: JankoGroupJ4
PlaintextUsage: JankoGroupJ4[] represents the sporadic simple Janko group J4.

Name: JarqueBeraALMTest
PlaintextUsage:
JarqueBeraALMTest[data] tests whether data is normally distributed using the Jarque–Bera ALM test.
JarqueBeraALMTest[data, "property"] returns the value of "property".

Name: JohnsonDistribution
PlaintextUsage:
JohnsonDistribution["SB", γ, δ, μ, σ] represents a bounded Johnson distribution with shape parameters γ, δ, location parameter μ, and scale parameter σ.
JohnsonDistribution["SL", γ, δ, μ, σ] represents a semi-bounded Johnson distribution.
JohnsonDistribution["SU", γ, δ, μ, σ] represents an unbounded Johnson distribution.
JohnsonDistribution["SN", γ, δ, μ, σ] represents a normal Johnson distribution.

Name: Join
PlaintextUsage:
Join[list1, list2, …] concatenates lists or other expressions that share the same head.
Join[list1, list2, …, n] joins the objects at level n in each of the listi.

Name: JoinAcross
PlaintextUsage:
JoinAcross[{a1, a2, …}, {b1, b2, …}, keyspec] gives a list of associations obtained by joining those pairs of associations ai and bj in which the values specified by keyspec match.
JoinAcross[tab1, tab2, keyspec] joins two tabular objects according to keyspec.
JoinAcross[prefix1obj1, prefix2obj2, keyspec] prefixes the keys in obji with prefixi using ExtendedKey[prefixi, ckeyij].
JoinAcross[alist, blist, keyspec, "joinspec"] uses joinspec to determine when to allow associations that contain missing elements to be generated.

Name: JoinForm
PlaintextUsage: JoinForm[type] is a graphics directive that specifies what type of joins should be used to connect segments of lines, tubes, edges, and related primitives.

Name: Joined
PlaintextUsage: Joined is an option for ListPlot and related functions that specifies whether points in each dataset should be joined into a line, or should be plotted as separate points.

Name: JoinedCurve
PlaintextUsage:
JoinedCurve[{segment1, segment2, …}] represents a curve consisting of segment1 followed by segment2 etc. 
JoinedCurve[{component1, component2, …}] represents a list of separate component curves component1, component2, etc.

Name: JordanDecomposition
PlaintextUsage: JordanDecomposition[m] yields the Jordan decomposition of a square matrix m. The result is a list {s, j} where s is a similarity matrix and j is the Jordan canonical form of m.

Name: JordanMatrix
PlaintextUsage:
JordanMatrix[λ, n] returns a Jordan matrix with dimension n and diagonal elements λ.
JordanMatrix[λ, n, dir] returns a Jordan matrix oriented by specification dir.

Name: JordanModelDecomposition
PlaintextUsage: JordanModelDecomposition[ssm] yields the Jordan decomposition of the state-space model ssm.

Name: JuliaSetBoettcher
PlaintextUsage: JuliaSetBoettcher[c, z] gives the Böttcher coordinate of z with respect to the quadratic Julia set Jc.

Name: JuliaSetIterationCount
PlaintextUsage:
JuliaSetIterationCount[f, z, p] returns the number of iterations, beginning with the complex number zp, of the function f(z) needed to determine whether p is in the Julia set of f.
JuliaSetIterationCount[c, p] returns the number of iterations, beginning with the complex number zp, of the function f(z)z^2+c needed to determine whether p is in the Julia set of f(z)z^2+c.
JuliaSetIterationCount[f, z, {p1, p2, …}] returns a list of the number of iterations required to determine whether each member of {p1, p2, …} is in the Julia set of f.
JuliaSetIterationCount[c, {p1, p2, …}] returns a list of the number of iterations required to determine whether each member of {p1, p2, …} is in the Julia set of f(z)z^2+c.

Name: JuliaSetPlot
PlaintextUsage:
JuliaSetPlot[f, z] plots the Julia set of the rational function f of the variable z.
JuliaSetPlot[c] plots the Julia set of the function f(z)z^2+c.

Name: JuliaSetPoints
PlaintextUsage:
JuliaSetPoints[f, z] returns a list of coordinates approximating the real and imaginary parts of the complex numbers in the Julia set of the rational function f of the variable z.
JuliaSetPoints[c] returns a list of coordinates of points approximating the Julia set of the function f(z)z^2+c.

Name: JulianDate
PlaintextUsage:
JulianDate[] gives the current number of days since noon on November 24, 4714 BCE in the GMT time zone. 
JulianDate[date] gives the number of days for the specified date.
JulianDate["type"] gives the Julian date variant of the specified type.
JulianDate["type", date] gives the variant for the specified date.

Name: KCoreComponents
PlaintextUsage:
KCoreComponents[g, k] gives the k-core components of the underlying simple graph of g.
KCoreComponents[g, k, "In"] gives the k-core components with vertex in-degrees at least k.
KCoreComponents[g, k, "Out"] gives the k-core components with vertex out-degrees at least k.
KCoreComponents[{vw, …}, …] uses rules vw to specify the graph g.

Name: KDistribution
PlaintextUsage: KDistribution[ν, w] represents a K distribution with shape parameters ν and w.

Name: KEdgeConnectedComponents
PlaintextUsage:
KEdgeConnectedComponents[g, k] gives the k-edge-connected components of the graph g.
KEdgeConnectedComponents[g, k, {v1, v2, …}] gives the k-edge-connected components that include at least one of the vertices v1, v2, ….
KEdgeConnectedComponents[{vw, …}, …] uses rules vw to specify the graph g.

Name: KEdgeConnectedGraphQ
PlaintextUsage: KEdgeConnectedGraphQ[g, k] yields True if the graph g is k-edge-connected and False otherwise.

Name: KVertexConnectedComponents
PlaintextUsage:
KVertexConnectedComponents[g, k] gives the k-vertex-connected components of the graph g.
KVertexConnectedComponents[g, k, {v1, v2, …}] gives the k-vertex-connected components that include at least one of the vertices v1, v2, … .

Name: KVertexConnectedGraphQ
PlaintextUsage: KVertexConnectedGraphQ[g, k] yields True if the graph g is k-vertex-connected and False otherwise.

Name: KagiChart
PlaintextUsage:
KagiChart[{{date1, p1}, {date2, p2}, …}] makes a Kagi chart with prices pi at date datei.
KagiChart[{"name", daterange}] makes a Kagi chart of closing prices for the financial entity "name" over the date range daterange.
KagiChart[{…}, rt] makes a Kagi chart with reversal threshold rt.

Name: KaiserBesselWindow
PlaintextUsage: KaiserBesselWindow[x] represents a Kaiser–Bessel window function of x.

Name: KaiserWindow
PlaintextUsage:
KaiserWindow[x] represents a Kaiser window function of x.
KaiserWindow[x, α] uses the parameter α.

Name: KalmanEstimator
PlaintextUsage:
KalmanEstimator[ssm, {w, v}] constructs the Kalman estimator for the StateSpaceModel ssm with process and measurement noise covariance matrices w and v. 
KalmanEstimator[ssm, {w, v, h}] includes the cross-covariance matrix h.
KalmanEstimator[{ssm, sensors}, {…}] specifies sensors as the noisy measurements of ssm.
KalmanEstimator[{ssm, sensors, dinputs}, {…}] specifies dinputs as the deterministic inputs of ssm.

Name: KalmanFilter
PlaintextUsage: KalmanFilter[tproc, data] filters data using the time series model given by tproc.

Name: KarhunenLoeveDecomposition
PlaintextUsage:
KarhunenLoeveDecomposition[{a1, a2, …}] gives the Karhunen–Loeve transform {{b1, b2, …}, m} of the numerical arrays {a1, a2, …}, where m.aibi. 
KarhunenLoeveDecomposition[{b1, b2, …}, m] uses the inverse of the matrix m for transforming bi to ai.

Name: KaryTree
PlaintextUsage:
KaryTree[n] gives a binary tree with n vertices.
KaryTree[n, k] gives a k-ary tree with n vertices.

Name: KatzCentrality
PlaintextUsage:
KatzCentrality[g, α] gives a list of Katz centralities for the vertices in the graph g and weight α.
KatzCentrality[g, α, β] gives a list of Katz centralities using weight α and initial centralities β.
KatzCentrality[{vw, …}, …] uses rules vw to specify the graph g.

Name: KeepExistingVersion
PlaintextUsage: KeepExistingVersion is an option for PacletInstall and PacletInstallSubmit that specifies whether an older version of a paclet should remain installed when a newer one gets installed.

Name: KelvinBei
PlaintextUsage:
KelvinBei[z] gives the Kelvin function bei (z).
KelvinBei[n, z] gives the Kelvin function bein (z).

Name: KelvinBer
PlaintextUsage:
KelvinBer[z] gives the Kelvin function ber (z).
KelvinBer[n, z] gives the Kelvin function bern (z).

Name: KelvinKei
PlaintextUsage:
KelvinKei[z] gives the Kelvin function kei (z).
KelvinKei[n, z] gives the Kelvin function kein (z).

Name: KelvinKer
PlaintextUsage:
KelvinKer[z] gives the Kelvin function ker (z).
KelvinKer[n, z] gives the Kelvin function kern (z).

Name: KendallTau
PlaintextUsage:
KendallTau[v1, v2] gives Kendall's rank correlation coefficient τ for the vectors v1 and v2.
KendallTau[m] gives Kendall's rank correlation coefficients τ for the matrix m.
KendallTau[m1, m2] gives Kendall's rank correlation coefficients τ for the matrices m1 and m2.
KendallTau[dist] gives Kendall's rank correlation matrix for the multivariate symbolic distribution dist.
KendallTau[dist, i, j] gives the (i, j)^th Kendall rank correlation for the multivariate symbolic distribution dist.

Name: KendallTauTest
PlaintextUsage:
KendallTauTest[v1, v2] tests whether the vectors v1 and v2 are independent.
KendallTauTest[m1, m2] tests whether the matrices m1 and m2 are independent.
KendallTauTest[…, "property"] returns the value of "property".

Name: KernelConfiguration
PlaintextUsage: KernelConfiguration[spec] specifies a kernel that can be used for RemoteEvaluate or LaunchKernels.

Name: KernelConfigurationEdit
PlaintextUsage:
KernelConfigurationEdit[kernelspec] gives a dialog for editing the properties of a new kernel specification based on kernelspec.
KernelConfigurationEdit[] prompts for the type of kernel to edit.

Name: KernelEvaluate
PlaintextUsage:
KernelEvaluate[expr] evaluates expr in the Wolfram Language kernel, even when called from compiled code.
KernelEvaluate[x, expr] captures the value of the compiled variable x for use in the evaluation of expr. 
KernelEvaluate[{x1, x2, …}, expr] captures the values of the xi for use in the evaluation of expr.

Name: KernelFunction
PlaintextUsage: KernelFunction[f] represents a function to be evaluated in the Wolfram Language kernel, even when called from compiled code.

Name: KernelMixtureDistribution
PlaintextUsage:
KernelMixtureDistribution[{x1, x2, …}] represents a kernel mixture distribution based on the data values xi.
KernelMixtureDistribution[{{x1, y1, …}, {x2, y2, …}, …}] represents a multivariate kernel mixture distribution based on data values {xi, yi, …}.
KernelMixtureDistribution[…, bw] represents a kernel mixture distribution with bandwidth bw.
KernelMixtureDistribution[…, bw, ker] represents a kernel mixture distribution with bandwidth bw and smoothing kernel ker.

Name: KernelModelFit
PlaintextUsage:
KernelModelFit[data] fits the given dataset data using a default local kernel.
KernelModelFit[data, bw] uses bandwidth bw for the kernel function.
KernelModelFit[data, bw, f] uses the specified local kernel f.

Name: KernelObject
PlaintextUsage: KernelObject[…] represents a kernel available for parallel computing.

Name: Ket
PlaintextUsage: Ket[{k1, k2, …}] displays as |k1, k2, …〉.

Name: Key
PlaintextUsage:
Key[key] represents a key used to access a value in an association or a column in a Tabular object.
Key[key][assoc] extracts the value corresponding to key in the association assoc.

Name: KeyCollisionFunction
PlaintextUsage: KeyCollisionFunction is an option for JoinAcross that specifies how to handle pairs of elements that are not being joined but nevertheless have the same key.

Name: KeyComplement
PlaintextUsage: KeyComplement[{assocall, assoc1, assoc2, …}] generates an association in which only elements whose keys appear in assocall but not in any of the associ are retained.

Name: KeyDrop
PlaintextUsage:
KeyDrop[assoc, {key1, key2, …}] yields an association from which elements with keys keyi have been dropped. 
KeyDrop[{assoc1, assoc2, …}, keys] gives a list of associations.
KeyDrop[keys] represents an operator form of KeyDrop that can be applied to an expression.

Name: KeyDropFrom
PlaintextUsage:
KeyDropFrom[a, key] changes the association a by dropping the element with the specified key.
KeyDropFrom[a, {key1, key2, …}] drops the elements with keys keyi.

Name: KeyExistsQ
PlaintextUsage:
KeyExistsQ[assoc, key] returns True if the specified key exists in the association assoc, and False otherwise.
KeyExistsQ[key] represents an operator form of KeyExistsQ that can be applied to an expression.

Name: KeyFreeQ
PlaintextUsage:
KeyFreeQ[assoc, form] yields True if no key in the association assoc matches form, and yields False otherwise.
KeyFreeQ[form] represents an operator form of KeyFreeQ that can be applied to an expression.

Name: KeyIntersection
PlaintextUsage: KeyIntersection[{assoc1, assoc2, …}] generates a list of associations in which only elements whose keys appear in all the associ are retained.

Name: KeyMap
PlaintextUsage:
KeyMap[f, key1val1, key2val2, …] maps f over the keys in an association, giving f[key1]val1, f[key2]val2, ….
KeyMap[f] represents an operator form of KeyMap that can be applied to an expression.

Name: KeyMemberQ
PlaintextUsage:
KeyMemberQ[assoc, form] yields True if a key in the association assoc matches form, and False otherwise.
KeyMemberQ[form] represents an operator form of KeyMemberQ that can be applied to an expression.

Name: KeySelect
PlaintextUsage:
KeySelect[assoc, crit] selects elements in the association assoc for which crit applied to their keys is True.
KeySelect[crit] represents an operator form of KeySelect that can be applied to an expression.

Name: KeySort
PlaintextUsage:
KeySort[assoc] orders the elements of an association by sorting its keys.
KeySort[assoc, p] orders the elements of an association using the ordering function p.

Name: KeySortBy
PlaintextUsage:
KeySortBy[assoc, f] sorts the elements of an association in the order defined by applying f to each of their keys.
KeySortBy[f] represents an operator form of KeySortBy that can be applied to an expression.

Name: KeyTake
PlaintextUsage:
KeyTake[assoc, {key1, key2, …}] yields an association containing only the elements with keys keyi.
KeyTake[{assoc1, assoc2, …}, keys] gives a list of associations.
KeyTake[{key1, key2, …}] represents an operator form of KeyTake that can be applied to an expression.

Name: KeyUnion
PlaintextUsage:
KeyUnion[{assoc1, assoc2, …}] generates a list of associations in which each association has the union of the keys of the associ, padding by inserting values of Missing[…] if necessary.
KeyUnion[{assoc1, assoc2, …}, f] uses f[key] as the value associated with a missing key.

Name: KeyValueMap
PlaintextUsage:
KeyValueMap[f, key1val1, key2val2, …] gives the list {f[key1, val1], f[key2, val2], …}.
KeyValueMap[f] represents an operator form of KeyValueMap that can be applied to an expression.

Name: KeyValuePattern
PlaintextUsage: KeyValuePattern[{patt1, …}] is a pattern object that represents an association or list of rules that includes elements matching each of the patti.

Name: KeyframeActions
PlaintextUsage: KeyframeActions is an option for Manipulate and related functions that gives a list of times and control settings.

Name: KeypointStrength
PlaintextUsage: KeypointStrength is an option for ImageKeypoints and related functions to specify a minimum strength of detected keypoints.

Name: Keys
PlaintextUsage:
Keys[key1val1, key2val2, …] gives a list of the keys keyi in an association.
Keys[{key1val1, key2val2, …}] gives a list of the keyi in a list of rules.
Keys[expr, h] gives a list of keys in expr, wrapping each of them with head h before evaluation.

Name: Khinchin
PlaintextUsage: Khinchin is Khinchin's constant, with numerical value ≃2.68545.

Name: KillProcess
PlaintextUsage: KillProcess[proc] kills the external process represented by the ProcessObject proc.

Name: KirchhoffGraph
PlaintextUsage:
KirchhoffGraph[kmat] gives the graph with Kirchhoff matrix kmat.
KirchhoffGraph[{v1, v2, …}, kmat] gives the graph with vertices vi and Kirchhoff matrix kmat.

Name: KirchhoffMatrix
PlaintextUsage:
KirchhoffMatrix[g] gives the Kirchhoff matrix of the graph g.
KirchhoffMatrix[{vw, …}] uses rules vw to specify the graph g.

Name: KleinInvariantJ
PlaintextUsage: KleinInvariantJ[τ] gives the Klein invariant modular elliptic function J (τ).

Name: KnapsackSolve
PlaintextUsage:
KnapsackSolve[{cost1, cost2, …}, maxtotalcost] solves the knapsack problem of finding the maximum number of items associated with each of the costi, subject to the constraint that the total cost is not larger than maxtotalcost.
KnapsackSolve[{{payoff1, cost1}, {payoff2, cost2}, …}, maxtotalcost] finds a number of items that maximizes the total payoff, while satisfying the constraint on the total cost.
KnapsackSolve[{{payoff1, cost1, maxcount1}, …}, maxtotalcost] allows at most maxcounti copies of item i.
KnapsackSolve[items, {maxtotalpayoff, maxtotalcost}] finds a result that gives a total payoff not larger than maxtotalpayoff.
KnapsackSolve[items, {maxtotalpayoff, maxtotalcost, maxtotalcount}] adds the constraint of having no more than maxtotalcount items in total. 
KnapsackSolve[label1itemspec1, …, maxtotals] labels each type of item and gives the result as an association.

Name: KnightTourGraph
PlaintextUsage: KnightTourGraph[m, n] gives a Knight's tour graph on an mn chessboard.

Name: KnotData
PlaintextUsage:
KnotData[knot, "property"] gives the specified property for a knot.
KnotData[knot] gives an image of the knot.
KnotData["class"] gives a list of knots in the specified class.

Name: KnownUnitQ
PlaintextUsage:
KnownUnitQ[expr] returns True if expr is a canonical unit, and False otherwise.
KnownUnitQ[expr, dims] gives True if expr is a canonical unit with physical dimensions dims, and False otherwise.

Name: KochCurve
PlaintextUsage:
KochCurve[n] gives the line segments representing the n ^th-step Koch curve.
KochCurve[n, {θ1, θ2, …}] takes a series of steps of unit length at successive relative angles θi. 
KochCurve[n, {{r1, θ1}, {r2, θ2}, …}] takes successive steps of lengths proportional to ri.

Name: KolmogorovSmirnovTest
PlaintextUsage:
KolmogorovSmirnovTest[data] tests whether data is normally distributed using the Kolmogorov–Smirnov test.
KolmogorovSmirnovTest[data, dist] tests whether data is distributed according to dist using the Kolmogorov–Smirnov test.
KolmogorovSmirnovTest[data, dist, "property"] returns the value of "property".

Name: KroneckerDelta
PlaintextUsage: KroneckerDelta[n1, n2, …] gives the Kronecker delta δ n1 n2 …, equal to 1 if all the ni are equal, and 0 otherwise.

Name: KroneckerModelDecomposition
PlaintextUsage: KroneckerModelDecomposition[ssm] yields the Kronecker decomposition of a descriptor state-space model ssm.

Name: KroneckerProduct
PlaintextUsage: KroneckerProduct[m1, m2, …] constructs the Kronecker product of the arrays mi.

Name: KroneckerSymbol
PlaintextUsage: KroneckerSymbol[n, m] gives the Kronecker symbol (n/m).

Name: KuiperTest
PlaintextUsage:
KuiperTest[data] tests whether data is normally distributed using the Kuiper test.
KuiperTest[data, dist] tests whether data is distributed according to dist using the Kuiper test.
KuiperTest[data, dist, "property"] returns the value of "property".

Name: KumaraswamyDistribution
PlaintextUsage: KumaraswamyDistribution[α, β] represents a Kumaraswamy distribution with shape parameters α and β.

Name: Kurtosis
PlaintextUsage:
Kurtosis[data] gives the coefficient of kurtosis for the elements in data.
Kurtosis[dist] gives the coefficient of kurtosis for the distribution dist.

Name: KuwaharaFilter
PlaintextUsage: KuwaharaFilter[data, r] computes for each element p in data the variance of the values in the four (r+1)×(r+1) squares that have p as a corner, and replaces p with the mean of the values of the square with least variance.

Name: LABColor
PlaintextUsage:
LABColor[l, a, b] represents a color in the CIELAB color space with lightness l and color components a and b. 
LABColor[l, a, b, α] specifies opacity α. 
LABColor["string"] returns a color from an HTML color name etc.
LABColor[color] returns the CIELAB representation of color.

Name: LCHColor
PlaintextUsage:
LCHColor[l, c, h] represents a color in the LCH color space with lightness l, chroma c and hue h.
LCHColor[l, c, h, a] specifies opacity a. 
LCHColor["string"] returns a color from an HTML color name etc.
LCHColor[color] returns the LCH representation of color.

Name: LCM
PlaintextUsage: LCM[n1, n2, …] gives the least common multiple of the ni.

Name: LLMConfiguration
PlaintextUsage:
LLMConfiguration[…] represents a configuration for an LLM.
LLMConfiguration[propval] creates a configuration based on $LLMEvaluator with the specified property set to val.
LLMConfiguration[<|prop1->val1, prop2->val2, ...|>] specifies several properties and values.
LLMConfiguration[LLMConfiguration[…], propspec] creates a configuration based on an existing configuration.

Name: LLMEvaluator
PlaintextUsage: LLMEvaluator is an option for functions such as LLMSynthesize that specifies the LLM configuration.

Name: LLMExampleFunction
PlaintextUsage:
LLMExampleFunction[{in1out1, in2out2, …}] creates an LLMFunction from few-shot examples.
LLMExampleFunction[{in1, in2, …}{out1, out2, …}] generates the same result.
LLMExampleFunction[{header, training}] prefaces the prompt with header.
LLMExampleFunction[prompting, form] includes the interpreter form to apply to the response.

Name: LLMFunction
PlaintextUsage:
LLMFunction[prompt] represents a template for a large language model (LLM) prompt.
LLMFunction[{prompt1, prompt2, …}] represents a combination of multiple prompts.
LLMFunction[prompt, form] includes the interpreter form to apply to the response.
LLMFunction[…][params] give the LLM service response for prompt applied to parameters params.

Name: LLMGraph
PlaintextUsage:
LLMGraph[name1fun1, …] creates an LLMGraph where node "namei" evaluates funi on parent nodes' outputs.
LLMGraph[…][input] gives the result of running the graph on input.
LLMGraph[…][input, prop] gives the property prop after running the graph on input.

Name: LLMGraphSubmit
PlaintextUsage:
LLMGraphSubmit[LLMGraph[…], input] evaluates an LLMGraph asynchronously on the input input.
LLMGraphSubmit[LLMGraph[…], input, target] specifies the outputs to compute.

Name: LLMPrompt
PlaintextUsage:
LLMPrompt["name"] gives the TemplateObject for the specified large language model prompt.
LLMPrompt[resource] retrieves the TemplateObject for the specified resource.
LLMPrompt[…, params] gives the TemplateObject with slots filled in by params.
LLMPrompt[…][p1, p2, …] applies a template with numbered slots to parameter values pi.
LLMPrompt[…][key1p1, key2p2] applies a template with named slots to parameter data.

Name: LLMPromptGenerator
PlaintextUsage:
LLMPromptGenerator[f] represents a prompt generator that uses the function f.
LLMPromptGenerator[f, inputspec] provides the specified inputspec to f.

Name: LLMResourceFunction
PlaintextUsage:
LLMResourceFunction["name"] retrieves an LLMFunction with the specified name.
LLMResourceFunction[loc] imports an LLMFunction from the specified location.
LLMResourceFunction[…][params] applies the specified LLMFunction to the parameters params.

Name: LLMResourceTool
PlaintextUsage:
LLMResourceTool[name] gives the TemplateObject for the specified large language model tool.
LLMResourceTool[resource] retrieves the TemplateObject for the specified resource.
LLMResourceTool[…, <|key1p1, key2p2, …|>] gives the TemplateObject with slots filled in by parameters.
LLMResourceTool[…][<|key1p1, key2p2, …|>] creates an LLMTool by applying the template to parameter data.

Name: LLMSynthesize
PlaintextUsage:
LLMSynthesize[prompt] generates text according to the input prompt.
LLMSynthesize[{prompt1, …}] combines multiple prompti together.
LLMSynthesize[…, prop] returns the specified property of the generated text.

Name: LLMSynthesizeSubmit
PlaintextUsage:
LLMSynthesizeSubmit[prompt] generates text asynchronously according to the input prompt.
LLMSynthesizeSubmit[{prompt1, …}] combines multiple prompti together.

Name: LLMTool
PlaintextUsage:
LLMTool["name", params, fun] represents a tool for use by an LLM enabling it to run fun on parameters described by params.
LLMTool[{"name", "description"}, params, fun] uses a description to prompt the LLM.

Name: LLMToolRequest
PlaintextUsage:
LLMToolRequest[…] represents a tool request made by an LLM.
LLMToolRequest["tool", {name1->val1, name2->val2, …}] represents a request to "tool" with the specified parameter values.
LLMToolRequest["tool", params, str] annotates a request with the request string.

Name: LLMToolResponse
PlaintextUsage: LLMToolResponse[…] represents a response to an LLM tool request.

Name: LQEstimatorGains
PlaintextUsage:
LQEstimatorGains[ssm, {w, v}] gives the optimal estimator gain matrix for the StateSpaceModel ssm, with process and measurement noise covariance matrices w and v.
LQEstimatorGains[ssm, {w, v, h}] includes the cross-covariance matrix h.
LQEstimatorGains[{ssm, sensors}, {…}] specifies sensors as the noisy measurements of ssm.
LQEstimatorGains[{ssm, sensors, dinputs}, {…}] specifies dinputs as the deterministic inputs of ssm.

Name: LQGRegulator
PlaintextUsage:
LQGRegulator[sspec, cvs, wts] gives the optimal output feedback controller for the stochastic system specification sspec with noise covariance matrices cvs that minimizes a cost function with weights wts.
LQGRegulator[…, "prop"] gives the value of the property "prop".

Name: LQOutputRegulatorGains
PlaintextUsage:
LQOutputRegulatorGains[sspec, wts] gives the state feedback gains for the system specification sspec that minimizes an output cost function with weights wts.
LQOutputRegulatorGains[…, "prop"] gives the value of the property "prop".

Name: LQRegulatorGains
PlaintextUsage:
LQRegulatorGains[sspec, wts] gives the state feedback gains for the system specification sspec that minimizes a cost function with weights wts.
LQRegulatorGains[…, "prop"] gives the value of the property "prop".

Name: LUDecomposition
PlaintextUsage: LUDecomposition[m] generates a representation of the LU decomposition of a square matrix m.

Name: LUVColor
PlaintextUsage:
LUVColor[l, u, v] represents a color in the LUV color space with lightness l and color components u and v.
LUVColor[l, u, v, a] specifies opacity a. 
LUVColor["string"] returns a color from an HTML color name etc.
LUVColor[color] returns the LUV representation of color.

Name: Label
PlaintextUsage: Label[tag] represents a point in a compound expression to which control can be transferred using Goto.

Name: LabelStyle
PlaintextUsage: LabelStyle is an option for formatting and related constructs that specifies the style to use in displaying their label-like elements.

Name: LabelVisibility
PlaintextUsage: LabelVisibility is an option for Callout and Labeled in plotting functions that determines which labels are shown.

Name: Labeled
PlaintextUsage:
Labeled[expr, lbl] displays expr labeled with lbl. 
Labeled[expr, lbl, pos] places lbl at a position specified by pos. 
Labeled[expr, {lbl1, lbl2, …}, {pos1, …}] places the lbli at positions posi. 
Labeled[expr, {lbl1, lbl2, lbl3, lbl4}, All] places the lbli at the bottom, left, top, and right, respectively.

Name: LabeledGraphicsBox
PlaintextUsage:
LabeledGraphicsBox[box, lbl] is a low-level construct that represents a graphics box with a label attached to it.
LabeledGraphicsBox[box, lbl, pos] places lbl at a position specified by pos.
LabeledGraphicsBox[box, {lbl1, lbl2, …}, {pos1, pos2, …}] places the lbli at positions posi.

Name: LabelingFunction
PlaintextUsage: LabelingFunction is an option for data visualization functions to automatically label elements of a visualization.

Name: LabelingSize
PlaintextUsage: LabelingSize is an option to visualization functions that specifies the size to be used for labels and callouts.

Name: LabelingTarget
PlaintextUsage: LabelingTarget is an option for visualization functions that specifies how many items are automatically labeled.

Name: LaguerreL
PlaintextUsage:
LaguerreL[n, x] gives the Laguerre polynomial Ln (x). 
LaguerreL[n, a, x] gives the generalized Laguerre polynomial L_n^a(x).

Name: LakeData
PlaintextUsage:
LakeData[entity, property] gives the value of the specified property for the lake entity.
LakeData[{entity1, entity2, …}, property] gives a list of property values for the specified lake entities.
LakeData[entity, property, annotation] gives the specified annotation associated with the given property.

Name: LambdaComponents
PlaintextUsage:
LambdaComponents[g] gives the lambda components of the graph g.
LambdaComponents[g, {v1, v2, …}] gives the lambda components that include at least one of the vertices {v1, v2, …}.
LambdaComponents[{vw, …}, …] uses rules vw to specify the graph g.

Name: LameC
PlaintextUsage: LameC[ν, j, z, m] gives the j ^th Lamé function Ec _ν^(j)(zm) of order ν with elliptic parameter m.

Name: LameCPrime
PlaintextUsage: LameCPrime[ν, j, z, m] gives the z-derivative of the j ^th Lamé function Ec _ν^(j)(zm) of order ν with elliptic parameter m.

Name: LameEigenvalueA
PlaintextUsage: LameEigenvalueA[ν, j, m] gives the j ^th Lamé eigenvalue a _ν^(j)(m) of order ν with elliptic parameter m for the function LameC[ν, j, z, m].

Name: LameEigenvalueB
PlaintextUsage: LameEigenvalueB[ν, j, m] gives the j ^th Lamé eigenvalue b _ν^(j)(m) of order ν with elliptic parameter m for the Lamé function LameS[ν, j, z, m].

Name: LameS
PlaintextUsage: LameS[ν, j, z, m] gives the j ^th Lamé function Es _ν^(j)(zm) of order ν with elliptic parameter m.

Name: LameSPrime
PlaintextUsage: LameSPrime[ν, j, z, m] gives the z-derivative of the j ^th Lamé function Es _ν^(j)(zm) of order ν with elliptic parameter m.

Name: LaminaData
PlaintextUsage:
LaminaData[entity, property] gives the value of the specified property for the lamina entity.
LaminaData[{entity1, entity2, …}, property] gives a list of property values for the specified lamina entities.
LaminaData[entity, property, annotation] gives the specified annotation associated with the given property.

Name: LanczosWindow
PlaintextUsage: LanczosWindow[x] represents a Lanczos window function of x.

Name: LandauDistribution
PlaintextUsage:
LandauDistribution[μ, σ] represents a Landau distribution with location parameter μ and scale parameter σ.
LandauDistribution[] represents a Landau distribution with location parameter 0 and scale parameter 1.

Name: Language
PlaintextUsage: Language is an option that specifies the language to use.

Name: LanguageCategory
PlaintextUsage: LanguageCategory is an option for Cell that determines in what category of language the contents of the cell should be assumed to be for purposes of spell checking and hyphenation.

Name: LanguageData
PlaintextUsage:
LanguageData[entity, property] gives the value of the specified property for the language entity.
LanguageData[{entity1, entity2, …}, property] gives a list of property values for the specified language entities.
LanguageData[entity, property, annotation] gives the specified annotation associated with the given property.

Name: LanguageIdentify
PlaintextUsage:
LanguageIdentify["string"] attempts to determine what human language text in string is in, predominantly.
LanguageIdentify[audio] performs language identification in audio recording audio.
LanguageIdentify[video] performs language identification of the audio track in video.

Name: LaplaceDistribution
PlaintextUsage:
LaplaceDistribution[μ, β] represents a Laplace double-exponential distribution with mean μ and scale parameter β.
LaplaceDistribution[] represents a Laplace double-exponential distribution with mean 0 and scale parameter 1.

Name: LaplaceTransform
PlaintextUsage:
LaplaceTransform[f[t], t, s] gives the symbolic Laplace transform of f[t] in the variable t and returns a transform F[s] in the variable s.
LaplaceTransform[f[t], t, Overscript[s, ^]] gives the numeric Laplace transform at the numerical value Overscript[s, ^].
LaplaceTransform[f[t1, …, tn], {t1, …, tn}, {s1, …, sn}] gives the multidimensional Laplace transform of f[t1, …, tn].

Name: Laplacian
PlaintextUsage:
Laplacian[f, {x1, …, xn}] gives the Laplacian ∂^2f/∂x1^2+…+∂^2f/∂xn^2.
Laplacian[f, {x1, …, xn}, chart] gives the Laplacian in the given coordinates chart.

Name: LaplacianFilter
PlaintextUsage:
LaplacianFilter[data, r] convolves data with a radius-r Laplacian kernel.
LaplacianFilter[data, {r1, r2, …}] uses radius ri at level i in data.

Name: LaplacianGaussianFilter
PlaintextUsage:
LaplacianGaussianFilter[data, r] convolves data with a Laplacian of Gaussian kernel of pixel radius r.
LaplacianGaussianFilter[data, {r, σ}]  convolves data with a Laplacian of Gaussian kernel of radius r and standard deviation σ.

Name: LaplacianPDETerm
PlaintextUsage:
LaplacianPDETerm[vars] represents a Laplacian term ∇^2{x1, …, xn}u with model variables vars.
LaplacianPDETerm[vars, pars] uses model parameters pars.

Name: Large
PlaintextUsage: Large is a style or option setting that specifies that objects should be large.

Name: Larger
PlaintextUsage: Larger is a style or option setting that specifies that objects should be larger.

Name: Last
PlaintextUsage:
Last[expr] gives the last element in expr. 
Last[expr, def] gives the last element if there are any elements, or def otherwise.

Name: Latitude
PlaintextUsage:
Latitude[pos] gives the latitude in degrees of a geographic position specified by pos.
Latitude[pos, datum] gives the latitude referring to the specified geodetic datum.

Name: LatitudeLongitude
PlaintextUsage:
LatitudeLongitude[pos] gives a list of the latitude and longitude in degrees of a geographic position specified by pos.
LatitudeLongitude[pos, datum] gives the latitude and longitude referring to the specified geodetic datum.

Name: LatticeData
PlaintextUsage:
LatticeData[lattice, "property"] gives the specified property for a lattice.
LatticeData[n] gives a list of named lattices of dimension n.

Name: LatticeReduce
PlaintextUsage: LatticeReduce[{v1, v2, …}] gives a reduced basis for the set of vectors vi.

Name: LaunchKernels
PlaintextUsage:
LaunchKernels[] launches all currently configured parallel subkernels.
LaunchKernels[n] launches n local subkernels on the current computer.
LaunchKernels[ker] launches the kernel specified by ker.
LaunchKernels[{ker1, ker2, …}] launches the kernels keri.

Name: LayerSizeFunction
PlaintextUsage: LayerSizeFunction is an option for TreePlot that gives a function to specify the relative height to allow for each layer.

Name: LayeredGraph
PlaintextUsage:
LayeredGraph[g] creates a graph with vertices and edges from the graph g represented as a layered plot.
LayeredGraph[{e1, e2, …}] creates a graph with edges ej represented as a layered plot.
LayeredGraph[{…, w[ei], …}] creates a graph with edges ei with features defined by the symbolic wrapper w.
LayeredGraph[…, vpos] places the dominant vertex v in the plot at position pos.

Name: LayeredGraph3D
PlaintextUsage:
LayeredGraph3D[g] creates a graph with vertices and edges from the graph g represented as a 3D layered plot.
LayeredGraph3D[{e1, e2, …}] creates a graph with edges ej represented as a 3D layered plot.
LayeredGraph3D[{…, w[ei], …}] creates a graph with edges ei with features defined by the symbolic wrapper w.
LayeredGraph3D[…, vpos] places the dominant vertex v in the plot at position pos.

Name: LayeredGraphPlot
PlaintextUsage:
LayeredGraphPlot[g] generates a layered plot of the graph g.
LayeredGraphPlot[{e1, e2, …}] generates a layered plot of the graph with edges ej.
LayeredGraphPlot[{…, w[ei], …}] plots ei with features defined by the symbolic wrapper w.
LayeredGraphPlot[{v i1v j1, …}] uses rules vikvjk to specify the graph g.
LayeredGraphPlot[m] uses the adjacency matrix m to specify the graph g.
LayeredGraphPlot[…, vpos] places the dominant vertex v in the plot at position pos.

Name: LayeredGraphPlot3D
PlaintextUsage:
LayeredGraphPlot3D[g] generates a 3D layered plot of the graph g.
LayeredGraphPlot3D[{e1, e2, …}] generates a 3D layered plot of the graph with edges ei.
LayeredGraphPlot3D[{…, w[ei], …}] plots ei with features defined by the symbolic wrapper w.
LayeredGraphPlot3D[{v i1v j1, …}] uses rules vikvjk to specify the graph g.
LayeredGraphPlot3D[m] uses the adjacency matrix m to specify the graph g.
LayeredGraphPlot3D[…, vpos] places the dominant vertex v in the plot at position pos.

Name: LeaderSize
PlaintextUsage: LeaderSize is an option for Callout that specifies what sizes to use for leader lines.

Name: LeafCount
PlaintextUsage: LeafCount[expr] gives the total number of indivisible subexpressions in expr.

Name: LeapVariant
PlaintextUsage: LeapVariant[n] represents a repeated calendar element caused by a leap period.

Name: LeapYearQ
PlaintextUsage: LeapYearQ[date] returns True if the year corresponding to date is a leap year.

Name: LearnDistribution
PlaintextUsage: LearnDistribution[{example1, example2, …}] generates a LearnedDistribution[…] that attempts to represent an underlying distribution for the examples given.

Name: LearnedDistribution
PlaintextUsage: LearnedDistribution[…] represents a distribution generated by LearnDistribution.

Name: LearningRate
PlaintextUsage: LearningRate is an option for NetTrain that specifies the rate at which to adjust neural net weights in order to minimize the training loss.

Name: LearningRateMultipliers
PlaintextUsage: LearningRateMultipliers is an option for net layers and for NetTrain, NetChain, NetGraph that specifies learning rate multipliers to apply during training.

Name: LeastSquares
PlaintextUsage:
LeastSquares[m, b] finds an x that solves the linear least-squares problem for the matrix equation m.x==b.
LeastSquares[a, b] finds an x that solves the linear least-squares problem for the array equation a.x==b.

Name: LeastSquaresFilterKernel
PlaintextUsage:
LeastSquaresFilterKernel[{{ω1, …, ω k-1}, {a1, …, ak}}, n] creates a k-band finite impulse response (FIR) filter kernel of length n designed using a least squares method, given the specified frequencies ωi and amplitudes ai.
LeastSquaresFilterKernel[{"type", spec}, n] uses the full filter specification {"type", spec}.

Name: Left
PlaintextUsage: Left is a symbol that represents the left-hand side for purposes of alignment and positioning.

Name: LeftArrow
PlaintextUsage: LeftArrow[x, y, …] displays as x←y←….

Name: LeftArrowBar
PlaintextUsage: LeftArrowBar[x, y, …] displays as x⇤y⇤….

Name: LeftArrowRightArrow
PlaintextUsage: LeftArrowRightArrow[x, y, …] displays as x⇆y⇆….

Name: LeftDownTeeVector
PlaintextUsage: LeftDownTeeVector[x, y, …] displays as x⥡y⥡….

Name: LeftDownVector
PlaintextUsage: LeftDownVector[x, y, …] displays as x⇃y⇃….

Name: LeftDownVectorBar
PlaintextUsage: LeftDownVectorBar[x, y, …] displays as x⥙y⥙….

Name: LeftJoinAcross
PlaintextUsage:
LeftJoinAcross[{a1, a2, …}, {b1, b2, …}, keyspec] gives a list of associations obtained by joining those pairs of associations ai and bj in which the values specified by keyspec match, including all unmatched entries from ai.
LeftJoinAcross[tab1, tab2, keyspec] joins two tabular objects according to keyspec, including all rows from tab1.
LeftJoinAcross[prefix1obj1, prefix2obj2, keyspec] prefixes the keys in obji with prefixi using ExtendedKey[prefixi, ckeyij].
LeftJoinAcross[obj, keyspec] represents an operator form of LeftJoinAcross that can be applied to another object.

Name: LeftRightArrow
PlaintextUsage: LeftRightArrow[x, y, …] displays as x↔y↔….

Name: LeftRightVector
PlaintextUsage: LeftRightVector[x, y, …] displays as x⥎y⥎….

Name: LeftTee
PlaintextUsage: LeftTee[x, y] displays as x⊣y.

Name: LeftTeeArrow
PlaintextUsage: LeftTeeArrow[x, y, …] displays as x↤y↤….

Name: LeftTeeVector
PlaintextUsage: LeftTeeVector[x, y, …] displays as x⥚y⥚….

Name: LeftTriangle
PlaintextUsage: LeftTriangle[x, y, …] displays as x⊲y⊲….

Name: LeftTriangleBar
PlaintextUsage: LeftTriangleBar[x, y, …] displays as x⧏y⧏….

Name: LeftTriangleEqual
PlaintextUsage: LeftTriangleEqual[x, y, …] displays as x⊴y⊴….

Name: LeftUpDownVector
PlaintextUsage: LeftUpDownVector[x, y, …] displays as x⥑y⥑….

Name: LeftUpTeeVector
PlaintextUsage: LeftUpTeeVector[x, y, …] displays as x⥠y⥠….

Name: LeftUpVector
PlaintextUsage: LeftUpVector[x, y, …] displays as x↿y↿….

Name: LeftUpVectorBar
PlaintextUsage: LeftUpVectorBar[x, y, …] displays as x⥘y⥘….

Name: LeftVector
PlaintextUsage: LeftVector[x, y, …] displays as x↼y↼….

Name: LeftVectorBar
PlaintextUsage: LeftVectorBar[x, y, …] displays as x⥒y⥒….

Name: LegendAppearance
PlaintextUsage: LegendAppearance is an option for charting functions that specifies the appearance of any legends that are generated.

Name: LegendFunction
PlaintextUsage: LegendFunction is an option for legends that specifies an overall function to apply to the generated legend.

Name: LegendLabel
PlaintextUsage: LegendLabel is an option for legends that specifies an overall label for a legend.

Name: LegendLayout
PlaintextUsage: LegendLayout is an option for legends that specifies how to format the legend content.

Name: LegendMargins
PlaintextUsage: LegendMargins is an option for legends that specifies the margins to leave around the legend.

Name: LegendMarkerSize
PlaintextUsage: LegendMarkerSize is an option for legends such as PointLegend that specifies the size of marker regions for each element.

Name: LegendMarkers
PlaintextUsage: LegendMarkers is an option for legends such as PointLegend that specifies markers for each element.

Name: Legended
PlaintextUsage:
Legended[expr, leg] displays expr with legend leg. 
Legended[expr, lbl] indicates in plotting and charting functions that a legend entry for expr should be created, with label lbl.

Name: LegendreP
PlaintextUsage:
LegendreP[n, x] gives the Legendre polynomial Pn (x). 
LegendreP[n, m, x] gives the associated Legendre polynomial P_n^m(x).

Name: LegendreQ
PlaintextUsage:
LegendreQ[n, z] gives the Legendre function of the second kind Qn (z). 
LegendreQ[n, m, z] gives the associated Legendre function of the second kind Q_n^m(z).

Name: Length
PlaintextUsage: Length[expr] gives the number of elements in expr.

Name: LengthWhile
PlaintextUsage: LengthWhile[list, crit] gives the number of contiguous elements ei starting at the beginning of list for which crit[ei] is True.

Name: LerchPhi
PlaintextUsage: LerchPhi[z, s, a] gives the Lerch transcendent Φ (z, s, a).

Name: Less
PlaintextUsage:
x<y yields True if x is determined to be less than y. 
x1<x2<x3 yields True if the xi form a strictly increasing sequence.

Name: LessEqual
PlaintextUsage:
x<=y or x≤y yields True if x is determined to be less than or equal to y.
x1≤x2≤x3 yields True if the xi form a nondecreasing sequence.

Name: LessEqualGreater
PlaintextUsage: LessEqualGreater[x, y, …] displays as x⋚y⋚….

Name: LessEqualThan
PlaintextUsage: LessEqualThan[y] is an operator form that yields x≤y when applied to an expression x.

Name: LessFullEqual
PlaintextUsage: LessFullEqual[x, y, …] displays as x≦y≦….

Name: LessGreater
PlaintextUsage: LessGreater[x, y, …] displays as x≶y≶….

Name: LessLess
PlaintextUsage: LessLess[x, y, …] displays as x≪y≪….

Name: LessSlantEqual
PlaintextUsage: LessSlantEqual[x, y, …] displays as x⩽y⩽….

Name: LessThan
PlaintextUsage: LessThan[y] is an operator form that yields x<y when applied to an expression x.

Name: LessTilde
PlaintextUsage: LessTilde[x, y, …] displays as x≲y≲….

Name: LetterCharacter
PlaintextUsage: LetterCharacter represents a letter character in StringExpression.

Name: LetterCounts
PlaintextUsage:
LetterCounts["string"] gives an association whose keys are the distinct letters in string, and whose values give the number of times those letters appear in string.
LetterCounts["string", n] gives counts of the distinct n-grams consisting of runs of n letters in string.
LetterCounts["string", n, {c1, c2, …}] allows the characters ci to appear in n-grams, in addition to ordinary letters.
LetterCounts[{string1, string2, …}, …] gives the counts for each of the stringi.

Name: LetterNumber
PlaintextUsage:
LetterNumber["c"] gives the position of the character c in the English alphabet.
LetterNumber["c", alpha] gives the position of c in the alphabet specified by alpha.
LetterNumber["string", …] gives a list of the positions of characters in string.

Name: LetterQ
PlaintextUsage: LetterQ[string] yields True if all the characters in the string are letters, and yields False otherwise.

Name: Level
PlaintextUsage:
Level[expr, levelspec] gives a list of all subexpressions of expr on levels specified by levelspec. 
Level[expr, levelspec, f] applies f to the sequence of subexpressions.

Name: LeveneTest
PlaintextUsage:
LeveneTest[data] tests whether the variance of data is 1. 
LeveneTest[{data1, data2, …}] tests whether the variances of data1, data2, … are equal.
LeveneTest[dspec, σ_0^2] tests a dispersion measure against σ_0^2.
LeveneTest[dspec, σ_0^2, "property"] returns the value of "property".

Name: LeviCivitaTensor
PlaintextUsage: LeviCivitaTensor[d] gives the d-dimensional Levi-Civita totally antisymmetric tensor.

Name: LevyDistribution
PlaintextUsage: LevyDistribution[μ, σ] represents a Lévy distribution with location parameter μ and dispersion parameter σ.

Name: LexicographicOrder
PlaintextUsage:
LexicographicOrder[{a1, a2, …}, {b1, b2, …}] gives Order[ai, bi] for the first non-coinciding pair ai, bi of elements, and 0 if the lists are identical.
LexicographicOrder[{a1, a2, …}, {b1, b2, …}, p] uses the ordering function p to compare ai with bi.
LexicographicOrder[p] represents an operator form that compares lists when applied to {a1, a2, …}, {b1, b2, …}.

Name: LexicographicSort
PlaintextUsage:
LexicographicSort[{e1, e2, …}] sorts the list of expressions ei in lexicographic order.
LexicographicSort[{e1, e2, …}, p] compares elements of the ei expressions using the ordering function p.

Name: LibraryDataType
PlaintextUsage:
LibraryDataType[datatype] specifies the data type for a LibraryFunction argument or result to be datatype.
LibraryDataType[datatype, etype] specifies an element type etype for data structures.
LibraryDataType[datatype, etype, d] specifies an array depth d for array data types.

Name: LibraryFunction
PlaintextUsage: LibraryFunction[args] represents a function that has been loaded from a Wolfram Library.

Name: LibraryFunctionDeclaration
PlaintextUsage:
LibraryFunctionDeclaration["extName", lib, type] represents a function declaration that exposes the library function extName with the type type from the library lib, for use in compiled code.
LibraryFunctionDeclaration[name->"extName", lib, type] aliases the function with name in compiled code.
LibraryFunctionDeclaration[nameSpec, type] assumes that the library will be loaded by the time the function is compiled.

Name: LibraryFunctionError
PlaintextUsage: LibraryFunctionError[name, code] represents an error returned from a LibraryFunction.

Name: LibraryFunctionInformation
PlaintextUsage: LibraryFunctionInformation[fun] returns information about a LibraryFunction.

Name: LibraryFunctionLoad
PlaintextUsage: LibraryFunctionLoad[lib, fun, argtype, rettype] loads Wolfram Library lib and makes the library function fun available in the Wolfram Language.

Name: LibraryFunctionUnload
PlaintextUsage: LibraryFunctionUnload[fun] unloads a LibraryFunction so that it cannot be used.

Name: LibraryLoad
PlaintextUsage: LibraryLoad[lib] loads the dynamic library lib into the Wolfram System runtime.

Name: LibraryUnload
PlaintextUsage: LibraryUnload[lib] unloads all functions that have been loaded from a Wolfram Library, then it unloads the library.

Name: LicenseEntitlementObject
PlaintextUsage:
LicenseEntitlementObject[…] represents an on-demand license entitlement.
LicenseEntitlementObject[id] gives the entitlement object representing the entitlement specified by id.

Name: LicenseEntitlements
PlaintextUsage: LicenseEntitlements[] gives a list of on-demand license entitlements owned by you.

Name: LicensingSettings
PlaintextUsage: LicensingSettings is an option for RemoteBatchSubmit and related functions to configure licensing for remote kernels.

Name: LiftingFilterData
PlaintextUsage: LiftingFilterData[…] represents lifting-filter data used to compute forward and inverse lifting wavelet transforms.

Name: LiftingWaveletTransform
PlaintextUsage:
LiftingWaveletTransform[data] gives the lifting wavelet transform (LWT) of an array of data.
LiftingWaveletTransform[data, wave] gives the lifting wavelet transform using the wavelet wave.
LiftingWaveletTransform[data, wave, r] gives the lifting wavelet transform using r levels of refinement.

Name: LightBlue
PlaintextUsage: LightBlue represents a light blue color in graphics or style specifications.

Name: LightBrown
PlaintextUsage: LightBrown represents a light brown color in graphics or style specifications.

Name: LightCyan
PlaintextUsage: LightCyan represents a light cyan color in graphics or style specifications.

Name: LightDark
PlaintextUsage: LightDark is an option for notebooks that specifies whether to display notebook contents in light or dark mode.

Name: LightDarkAutoColorRules
PlaintextUsage: LightDarkAutoColorRules is an option for Style that specifies how to map fixed colors from light to dark mode.

Name: LightDarkSwitched
PlaintextUsage:
LightDarkSwitched[lightcolor, darkcolor] displays lightcolor if used in a light mode notebook; otherwise, it displays darkcolor.
LightDarkSwitched[lightcolor, Automatic] uses an automatic dark color alternative for lightcolor.
LightDarkSwitched[Automatic, darkcolor] uses an automatic light color alternative for darkcolor.
LightDarkSwitched[lightcolor] is equivalent to LightDarkSwitched[lightcolor, Automatic].

Name: LightGray
PlaintextUsage: LightGray represents a light gray color in graphics or style specifications.

Name: LightGreen
PlaintextUsage: LightGreen represents a light green color in graphics or style specifications.

Name: LightMagenta
PlaintextUsage: LightMagenta represents a light magenta color in graphics or style specifications.

Name: LightOrange
PlaintextUsage: LightOrange represents a light orange color in graphics or style specifications.

Name: LightPink
PlaintextUsage: LightPink represents a light pink color in graphics or style specifications.

Name: LightPurple
PlaintextUsage: LightPurple represents a light purple color in graphics or style specifications.

Name: LightRed
PlaintextUsage: LightRed represents a light red color in graphics or style specifications.

Name: LightYellow
PlaintextUsage: LightYellow represents a light yellow color in graphics or style specifications.

Name: Lighter
PlaintextUsage:
Lighter[color] represents a lighter version of the specified color. 
Lighter[color, f] represents a version of the specified color lightened by a fraction f. 
Lighter[image, …] gives a lighter version of an image.
Lighter[video, …] gives a version of a video with lighter frames.

Name: Lighting
PlaintextUsage: Lighting is an option for Graphics3D and related functions that specifies what simulated lighting to use in coloring 3D surfaces.

Name: LightingAngle
PlaintextUsage: LightingAngle is an option for ReliefPlot and related functions that specifies the angle from which simulated illumination is taken to come.

Name: Likelihood
PlaintextUsage:
Likelihood[dist, {x1, x2, …}] gives the likelihood function for observations x1, x2, … from the distribution dist.
Likelihood[proc, {{t1, x1}, {t2, x2}, …}] gives the likelihood function for the observations xi at time ti from the process proc.
Likelihood[proc, {path1, path2, …}] gives the likelihood function for observations from path1, path2, … from the process proc.

Name: Limit
PlaintextUsage:
Limit[f, xx^*] gives the limit xx^*f(x). 
Limit[f, {x1x_1^*, …, xnx_n^*}] gives the nested limit _x1x_1^*⋯ _xnx_n^*f(x1, …, xn). 
Limit[f, {x1, …, xn}{x_1^*, …, x_n^*}] gives the multivariate limit _{x1, …, xn}{x_1^*, …, x_n^*}f(x1, …, xn).

Name: LimitsPositioning
PlaintextUsage: LimitsPositioning is an option for UnderoverscriptBox and related boxes that specifies whether to change the positioning of underscripts and overscripts in the way conventional for limits.

Name: LimitsPositioningTokens
PlaintextUsage: LimitsPositioningTokens is an option for selections that specifies a set of characters for which the option LimitsPositioning is set to True by default.

Name: LindleyDistribution
PlaintextUsage: LindleyDistribution[δ] represents a Lindley distribution with shape parameter δ.

Name: Line
PlaintextUsage:
Line[{p1, p2, …}] represents the line segments joining a sequence for points pi.
Line[{{p11, p12, …}, {p21, …}, …}] represents a collection of lines.

Name: LineBreakChart
PlaintextUsage:
LineBreakChart[{{date1, p1}, {date2, p2}, …}] makes a line break chart with prices pi at date datei.
LineBreakChart[{"name", daterange}] makes a line break chart of closing prices for the financial entity "name" over the date range daterange.
LineBreakChart[{…}, n] makes a line break chart where n bars in a row cause a reversal.

Name: LineBreakWithin
PlaintextUsage: LineBreakWithin is an option for selections that specifies whether line breaks occur automatically when the end of a line is reached.

Name: LineGraph
PlaintextUsage:
LineGraph[g] gives the line graph of the graph g.
LineGraph[{vw, …}] uses rules vw to specify the graph g.

Name: LineIndent
PlaintextUsage: LineIndent is an option for Style and Cell that specifies how many ems of indentation to add at the beginnings of lines for each level of nesting in an expression.

Name: LineIndentMaxFraction
PlaintextUsage: LineIndentMaxFraction is an option for Cell, StyleBox, and Style that specifies the maximum fraction of the total page width to indent at the beginnings of lines.

Name: LineIntegralConvolutionPlot
PlaintextUsage:
LineIntegralConvolutionPlot[{{vx, vy}, image}, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}] generates a line integral convolution plot of image convolved with the vector field {vx, vy} as a function of x and y.
LineIntegralConvolutionPlot[{vx, vy}, {x, xmin, xmax}, {y, ymin, ymax}] generates a line integral convolution plot of white noise with the vector field {vx, vy}.

Name: LineIntegralConvolutionScale
PlaintextUsage: LineIntegralConvolutionScale is an option to LineIntegralConvolutionPlot and related functions that determines the scale of the line integral convolution to be used.

Name: LineIntegrate
PlaintextUsage:
LineIntegrate[f, {x, y, …}∈curve] computes the scalar line integral of the function f[x, y, …] over the curve.
LineIntegrate[{p, q, …}, {x, y, …}∈curve] computes the vector line integral of the vector function {p[x, y, …], q[x, y, …], …}.

Name: LineLegend
PlaintextUsage:
LineLegend[{col1, …}, {lbl1, …}] generates a legend that associates color coli with label lbli.
LineLegend[{col1, …}, Automatic] generates a legend with placeholder labels for the colors coli.
LineLegend[{lbl1, …}] represents a legend with inherited colors within visualization functions.

Name: LineSpacing
PlaintextUsage: LineSpacing is an option for Style and Cell that specifies the spacing between successive lines of text.

Name: LinearFractionalOptimization
PlaintextUsage:
LinearFractionalOptimization[f, cons, vars] finds values of variables vars that minimize the linear fractional objective f subject to linear constraints cons.
LinearFractionalOptimization[{α, β, γ, δ}, {a, b}] finds a vector x that minimizes the linear fractional function (α.x+β)/(γ.x+δ) subject to the linear inequality constraints a.x+b⪰0. 
LinearFractionalOptimization[{α, β, γ, δ}, {a, b}, {aeq, beq}] includes the linear equality constraints aeq.x+beq0.
LinearFractionalOptimization[{α, β, γ, δ}, …, {dom1, dom2, …}] takes xi to be in the domain domi, where domi is Integers or Reals. 
LinearFractionalOptimization[…, "prop"] specifies what solution property "prop" should be returned.

Name: LinearFractionalTransform
PlaintextUsage:
LinearFractionalTransform[m] gives a TransformationFunction that represents a linear fractional transformation defined by the homogeneous matrix m. 
LinearFractionalTransform[{a, b, c, d}] represents a linear fractional transformation that maps r to (a.r+b)/(c.r+d).

Name: LinearGradientFilling
PlaintextUsage:
LinearGradientFilling[{col1, col2, …, coln}] is a two-dimensional graphics directive specifying that faces of polygons and other filled graphics objects are to be drawn using a progressive transition between colors coli along a straight horizontal line.
LinearGradientFilling[{pos1, pos2, …, posn}{col1, col2, …, coln}] uses the colors coli at the scaled positions posi.
LinearGradientFilling[{pos1, pos2, …, posn}{col1, col2, …, coln}, dir] draws along the straight line with a direction dir.
LinearGradientFilling[{pos1, …, posn}{col1, …, coln}, dir, padding] uses the specified padding when drawing beyond the boundary positions pos1 and posn.

Name: LinearGradientImage
PlaintextUsage:
LinearGradientImage[gcol] returns an image with values linearly changing from left to right based on gradient color gcol.
LinearGradientImage[{pos1, pos2}gcol] returns an image where the gradient starts at pos1 and ends at pos2.
LinearGradientImage[…, size] returns a linear gradient image of the specified size.
LinearGradientImage[…, size, "type"] gives an image converted to the specified type.

Name: LinearLayer
PlaintextUsage:
LinearLayer[n] represents a trainable, fully connected net layer that computes w.x+b with output vector of size n. 
LinearLayer[{n1, n2, …}] represents a layer that outputs an array of dimensions n1×n2×….
LinearLayer[] leaves the dimensions of the output array to be inferred from context.
LinearLayer[n, opts] includes options for initial weights and other parameters.

Name: LinearModelFit
PlaintextUsage:
LinearModelFit[{{x1, y1}, {x2, y2}, …}, {f1, f2, …}, x] constructs a linear model of the form β0+β1 f1+β2 f2+… that fits the yi for successive xi values.
LinearModelFit[data, {f1, f2, …}, {x1, x2, …}] constructs a linear model where the fi depend on the variables xk.
LinearModelFit[{m, v}] constructs a linear model from the design matrix m and response vector v.

Name: LinearOffsetFunction
PlaintextUsage: LinearOffsetFunction is an option for linear and generalized linear model fitting functions that specifies a component for the model that is to be assumed known.

Name: LinearOptimization
PlaintextUsage:
LinearOptimization[f, cons, vars] finds values of variables vars that minimize the linear objective f subject to linear constraints cons.
LinearOptimization[c, {a, b}]  finds a real vector x that minimizes the linear objective c.x subject to the linear inequality constraints a.x+b⪰0.
LinearOptimization[c, {a, b}, {aeq, beq}] includes the linear equality constraints aeq.x+beq0.
LinearOptimization[c, …, {dom1, dom2, …}] takes xi to be in the domain domi, where domi is Integers or Reals.
LinearOptimization[…, "prop"] specifies what solution property "prop" should be returned.

Name: LinearRecurrence
PlaintextUsage:
LinearRecurrence[ker, init, n] gives the sequence of length n obtained by iterating the linear recurrence with kernel ker starting with initial values init.
LinearRecurrence[ker, init, {n}] gives the n ^th term.
LinearRecurrence[ker, init, {nmin, nmax}] yields terms nmin through nmax.

Name: LinearSolve
PlaintextUsage:
LinearSolve[m, b] finds an x that solves the matrix equation m.x==b. 
LinearSolve[m] generates a LinearSolveFunction[…] that can be applied repeatedly to different b. 
LinearSolve[a, b] finds an x that solves the array equation a.x==b.

Name: LinearSolveFunction
PlaintextUsage: LinearSolveFunction[dimensions, data] represents a function for providing solutions to a matrix equation.

Name: LinearizingTransformationData
PlaintextUsage: LinearizingTransformationData[…] represents data of an AffineStateSpaceModel linearized by functions such as FeedbackLinearize and StateTransformationLinearize using transformation of variables.

Name: LinebreakAdjustments
PlaintextUsage: LinebreakAdjustments is an option for selections that sets parameters used for calculating where automatic line breaks should be inserted.

Name: LinkActivate
PlaintextUsage: LinkActivate[lnk] activates a WSTP connection, waiting for the program at the other end to respond.

Name: LinkClose
PlaintextUsage: LinkClose[link] closes an open WSTP connection.

Name: LinkConnect
PlaintextUsage: LinkConnect["name"] connects to a WSTP link created by another program.

Name: LinkCreate
PlaintextUsage:
LinkCreate["name"] creates a WSTP link with the specified name for another program to connect to. 
LinkCreate[] creates a WSTP link and picks an unused name for the link.

Name: LinkFunction
PlaintextUsage: LinkFunction is an option for GeneralizedLinearModelFit that specifies the link function for the generalized linear model.

Name: LinkInterrupt
PlaintextUsage: LinkInterrupt[link] sends an interrupt to the program at the other end of the specified WSTP connection.

Name: LinkLaunch
PlaintextUsage: LinkLaunch["prog"] starts the external program prog and opens a WSTP connection to it.

Name: LinkObject
PlaintextUsage: LinkObject["name", n1, n2] is an object that represents an active WSTP connection for functions such as LinkRead and LinkWrite.

Name: LinkPatterns
PlaintextUsage: LinkPatterns[link] gives a list of the patterns for which definitions were set up when the external program associated with the specified WSTP connection was installed.

Name: LinkProtocol
PlaintextUsage: LinkProtocol is an option to LinkLaunch, Install and related functions that specifies the underlying data transport protocol to use for a new WSTP link.

Name: LinkRankCentrality
PlaintextUsage:
LinkRankCentrality[g, α] gives the link-rank centralities for edges in the graph g and weight α.
LinkRankCentrality[g, α, β] gives the link-rank centralities, using weight α and initial vertex page-rank centralities β.
LinkRankCentrality[{vw, …}, …] uses rules vw to specify the graph g.

Name: LinkRead
PlaintextUsage:
LinkRead[link] reads one expression from the specified WSTP connection. 
LinkRead[link, h] wraps h around the expression read before evaluating it.

Name: LinkReadyQ
PlaintextUsage:
LinkReadyQ[link] tests whether there is an expression ready to read from the specified WSTP connection. 
LinkReadyQ[link, t] waits for up to t seconds to see if an expression becomes ready to read.
LinkReadyQ[{link1, link2, …}, t] tests all the linki in parallel, returning as soon as any of them are ready to read from.

Name: LinkWrite
PlaintextUsage: LinkWrite[link, expr] writes expr to the specified WSTP connection.

Name: Links
PlaintextUsage:
Links[] gives a list of all WSTP connections that are currently open. 
Links[patt] lists only links whose names match the specified string pattern.

Name: LiouvilleLambda
PlaintextUsage: LiouvilleLambda[n] gives the Liouville function λ (n).

Name: List
PlaintextUsage: {e1, e2, …} is a list of elements.

Name: ListAnimate
PlaintextUsage:
ListAnimate[{expr1, expr2, …}] generates an animation whose frames are the successive expri. 
ListAnimate[list, fps] displays fps frames per second.

Name: ListContourPlot
PlaintextUsage:
ListContourPlot[{{f11, …, f 1n}, …, {f m1, …, fmn}}] generates a contour plot from an array of values fij.
ListContourPlot[{{x1, y1, f1}, …, {xk, yk, fk}}] generates a contour plot from values fi specified at points {xi, yi}.

Name: ListContourPlot3D
PlaintextUsage:
ListContourPlot3D[farr] generates a contour plot from an array farr with values farr[[i, j, k]] at points {k, j, i}.
ListContourPlot3D[{{x1, y1, z1, f1}, {x2, y2, z2, f2}, …}] generates a contour plot from values fi at point {xi, yi, zi}.

Name: ListConvolve
PlaintextUsage:
ListConvolve[ker, list] forms the convolution of the kernel ker with list. 
ListConvolve[ker, list, k] forms the cyclic convolution in which the k ^th element of ker is aligned with each element in list. 
ListConvolve[ker, list, {kL, kR}] forms the cyclic convolution whose first element contains list[[1]]ker[[kL]] and whose last element contains list[[-1]]ker[[kR]]. 
ListConvolve[ker, list, klist, p] forms the convolution in which list is padded at each end with repetitions of the element p. 
ListConvolve[ker, list, klist, {p1, p2, …}] forms the convolution in which list is padded at each end with cyclic repetitions of the pi. 
ListConvolve[ker, list, klist, padding, g, h] forms a generalized convolution in which g is used in place of Times and h in place of Plus.
